I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn, and I grow wheat and corn. The soil here on the North China Plain is good for it. I have about 8 mu of contracted land. There's no question what I'll plant — winter wheat goes in October, summer maize goes right after I harvest the wheat in June. Same land, same rotation, every year. That's how we do it here.

For wheat, I use Jimai 22. I've used it for years. It doesn't fail me. I know how it grows. Before sowing I'll rotary till and put down the base fertilizer — diammonium phosphate and potash — then broadcast urea at topping stage after Chinese New Year when the plants start jointing. I'll irrigate at sowing if the soil is dry, then again before winter sets in, then at jointing, then at heading. Four times. That's what the wheat needs here. I'll spray herbicide in late winter and fungicide before heading — powdery mildew and rust come every year if you're not careful.

For maize, I'll buy hybrid seed from the village co-op — Zhengdan 958 or whatever they have that's similar and proven. I get it in the ground within a day or two of wheat harvest, before the soil dries out. I'll do a light rotary pass to break up the stubble, then seed it. Fertilizer goes down at planting as base, then I'll side-dress urea when it's about knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water here in summer — rains usually come — but I'll irrigate at planting and once during grain filling if it stays dry.

I won't try anything new this year. At 55, I know what works on my land.
